newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SHAREHOLDERS DROP SENTRACHEM LAW SUIT PLANS.
newsitem.headline: SHAREHOLDERS DROP SENTRACHEM LAW SUIT PLANS.

text.p: South African chemicals firm Sentrachem Ltd said on Monday that the action instituted against the firm by Yonbor Nominees (Pty) Ltd, a group of minority shareholders, had been withdrawn.

Sentrachem said in a statement that after constructive discussions this week the two parties had reached consensus and that the Nominees had accepted the explanation by Sentrachem concerning the difficult circumstances with which it found itself confronted.

Business Day newspaper said on Monday the potential law suit involved a 600,000 rand damages claim by the nominees against Sentrachem for its alleged failure to diclose in good time significant losses arising from ill-judged forward cover contracts at subsidiary Sanachem.

Sentrachem had issued a profit warning soon after reporting results for the 1996 year, saying the forward cover decisions would see it declare a loss for the six months to February, the paper said. Sentrachem subsequently declared a 217 million rand attributable loss for that period.
